extracted.intended_audience: Project Gutenberg volunteers, e-text transcribers, editors, and redistributors
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for preparing, formatting, and distributing a Project Gutenberg eBook (text transcription conventions plus legal/license requirements). Covers editorial choices (italics, capitalization, margin notes, Greek substitution, spelling) and Project Gutenberg licensing/redistribution rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transcriber's approach to capitalization and italics
rubrics_metrics.description: Restrict full capitalization to those places where Hobbes used it, except in chapter headings (which are fully capitalized here).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow original use of capitals where clear. For chapter headings, fully capitalize even if the original mixed capitalization and italics. This preserves the flavour of the original while making headings consistent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of italics used for quotations
rubrics_metrics.description: Where it is clear that the italics are to indicate the text is quoting, introduce quotation marks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Insert standard quotation marks around quoted passages; within those quotation marks retain the original capitalization Hobbes used. This change is permitted to make quotations clear in plain ASCII transcription.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of italics used for emphasis or proper names
rubrics_metrics.description: Where italics seem to be used for emphasis, or for proper names, capitalize the initial letter of the words instead of reproducing italics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not attempt to mark italics with underscores or slashes in plain vanilla ASCII; instead use initial-capitalization to approximate the emphasis or proper-name function of the original italics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion and formatting of margin notes
rubrics_metrics.description: When margin notes introduce paragraph subjects or word definitions, include them as headers to the paragraph, with all words having initial capitals and on a shortened line.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Convert margin notes into inline headers placed above the relevant paragraph to approximate the original function of margin notes (acting like an index). Keep them concise and capitalized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Placement of margin references to quotations
rubrics_metrics.description: For margin references to quotations, include them in the text in brackets immediately next to the quotation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If Hobbes included references in the main text, retain them as he put them, changing square brackets to round brackets only when necessary for clarity in plain ASCII.

rubrics_metrics.name: Greek alphabet and foreign-language handling
rubrics_metrics.description: For the Greek alphabet and other foreign alphabets, substitute the nearest ordinary letters and use initial capitals for foreign-language words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Replace non-ASCII characters (e.g., Greek letters) with nearest Latin-letter approximations so the text remains plain ASCII and readable, and capitalize foreign-language words' initial letters to indicate distinct terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve original spelling and punctuation where practicable
rubrics_metrics.description: Reproduce Hobbes' spelling and punctuation as exactly as possible, with the exception of introducing quotation marks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain eccentric spellings and punctuation that appear in the original to preserve historical flavor; limit editorial changes to those necessary for clarity in plain ASCII (e.g., quotation marks).

rubrics_metrics.name: Transcriber's editorial rationale (reading aloud)
rubrics_metrics.description: The transcriber found the text has more meaning when read aloud (sub-vocalization), and this guided editorial decisions about emphasis and punctuation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where emphasis and punctuation are eccentric, prefer renderings that preserve the performative sense of the original (as experienced when read aloud), within limits of plain-text format.

rubrics_metrics.description: The full Project Gutenberg License must accompany the work when distributed (see 'PLEASE READ THIS BEFORE YOU DISTRIBUTE OR USE THIS WORK').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not detach or remove the full license terms from any file containing part of this work. Whenever a Project Gutenberg work is accessed, displayed, performed, viewed, copied or distributed, the full license must be available with it.

rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever any copy of a Project Gutenberg work is accessed or distributed, the following sentence must appear prominently with active links or immediate access to the full license: "This eBook is for the use of anyone anywhere in the United States and most other parts of the world at no cost and with almost no restrictions whatsoever. If you are not located in the United States, you will have to check the laws of the country where you are located before using this eBook."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure that the exact sentence (or equivalent immediate access to it) is displayed prominently whenever the eBook or any associated file is made available. Provide active links to the full license when possible.

rubrics_metrics.description: "Project Gutenberg" is a registered trademark and may only be used on or associated with a work by people who agree to be bound by the terms of the license.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You may remove references to Project Gutenberg if the underlying work is public-domain and you do not wish to be bound by the trademark/licensing terms; otherwise, keep the Project Gutenberg attribution and comply with the license.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements when distributing in alternate formats
rubrics_metrics.description: If you provide the work in a format other than "Plain Vanilla ASCII" or the official posted format, you must, at no extra cost to the user, provide a copy or means to obtain the original plain format and include the full license.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distributors converting to binary, compressed, markup, or proprietary formats must also provide the original plain-text form upon request and include the full license text within the alternate-format distribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: No-fee distribution rule and exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not charge a fee for access to, viewing, displaying, performing, copying or distributing any Project Gutenberg works unless you comply with paragraph 1.E.8 or 1.E.9.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you intend to charge for copies or access, you must follow the fee rules (see 1.E.8: royalty payments, refund policies, defect replacement obligations) or obtain written permission per 1.E.9.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commercial redistribution fee and refund requirements (1.E.8)

rubrics_metrics.guidance: Calculate royalties per your normal tax methods; remit within 60 days of preparing tax returns. Clearly mark royalty payments and comply with refund/replacement obligations and all other free-distribution terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional terms for works posted with permission of copyright holder
rubrics_metrics.description: If an individual Project Gutenberg electronic work is posted with the permission of the copyright holder, redistribution must comply with both paragraphs 1.E.1–1.E.7 and any additional terms imposed by the copyright holder.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Link to or include any additional terms supplied by the copyright holder and ensure recipients are aware of both the Project Gutenberg license and these extra conditions.

rubrics_metrics.description: The copyright laws of the place where you are located govern what you can do with this work; Project Gutenberg makes no representations about copyright status outside the U.S.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you are outside the United States, check your local laws before downloading, copying, or creating derivative works. The Foundation's statements relate to U.S. copyright only.

rubrics_metrics.description: Except for the limited replacement/refund right in 1.F.3, Project Gutenberg and distributors disclaim all liability and provide the work 'AS-IS' without other warranties of merchantability or fitness for a purpose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distributors must include the warranty/disclaimer language. Users accept the work with the understanding there are no other remedies for defects except those described in paragraph 1.F.3.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited right of replacement or refund for defects (1.F.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: If you discover a defect within 90 days of receiving the work, you can receive a refund or replacement copy from the provider; electronic distributors may offer a second electronic copy before refund.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distributors must provide a replacement or refund procedure and honor defect reports within the 90-day window per the license terms. If a second copy is also defective, a refund must be issued on demand.

rubrics_metrics.description: Project Gutenberg eBooks are often created from several printed editions and volunteers expend effort to identify, research copyright, transcribe and proofread works not protected by U.S. copyright law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When distributing or modifying works, recognize the volunteer-based nature of Project Gutenberg; retain credits where practical and comply with license terms that protect the project and its mission.
